objective: Add conservative project/user-level retention and pruning for completed pi-swe initiatives, with durable completion timestamps, preview-first commands, safe treatment of tracked authority and durable artifacts, and less clutter in normal initiative discovery.

in: A versioned pi-swe config at the established global and project Pi config locations, with project overrides and disabled-by-default completed-initiative retention
A canonical completedAt lifecycle timestamp persisted when initiative finalization succeeds, with backward-compatible handling for existing completed authorities

A read-only prune planner that validates completed authorities, applies retention age, inventories directory contents, classifies tracked versus ignored/untracked material, and explains every eligible or skipped initiative
Explicit /swe prune --dry-run and /swe prune --apply surfaces plus equivalent structured-tool support, with dry-run as the default
A conservative deletion executor using store-grade path, symlink, lock, race, and durability safeguards
Default discovery/list behavior that hides completed initiatives from routine choices while preserving an explicit completed/history view
Focused destructive-boundary tests, documentation, and full repository qualification
out: Automatic deletion of tracked workflow authority or durable specs/plans/findings/reports
Automatic Git commits or pushes for prune deletions
Using filesystem mtime or ignored revision-log filenames as the durable completion clock
Pruning active, draft, paused, malformed, locked, symlinked, or concurrently changed initiatives
A parallel archive registry or second task ledger

constraints: Pi-swe remains the owner because it understands initiative validation, terminal status, locks, and authority paths; do not create a separate pruning extension or ledger.
Follow the existing pi-context configuration convention: safe bounded regular non-symlink global and project JSON files, project field overrides, bounded diagnostics, and fail-closed defaults.
Retention is disabled by default. Configuration is project/user-level, never stored in individual workflow authority.

Persist a canonical completedAt timestamp through finalization; existing completed schemaVersion 1 authorities without completedAt remain readable but are ineligible for age-based automatic pruning until an explicit compatibility rule is applied.
Dry-run is the default and must have no filesystem or Git side effects. Apply requires an explicit action and reports a bounded itemized result.
Automatic/background cleanup, if included after implementation review, is limited to ignored runtime logs; whole-initiative directory removal always requires explicit apply.

By default skip any initiative containing Git-tracked workflow authority or tracked/reviewable durable artifacts. includeTracked may make such entries visible as deletion candidates only after explicit apply, never silently remove or commit them.
Never delete noncanonical files, symlinks, active lock/temp files, or directories whose validated inventory changed between planning and apply.
Use stable parent-relative filesystem operations, cooperative locking, compare-and-swap inventory fingerprints, and directory sync analogous to InitiativeStore publication safeguards.
Prune output and autocomplete must remain bounded for repositories with many initiatives.
Normal initiative discovery hides complete authorities by default but status/open/history and explicit completed filters remain available.
Do not modify repository ignore policy as part of this feature.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Pi-swe loads a bounded versioned global/project configuration with retention disabled by default, project-over-global merging, clear diagnostics, and no per-initiative policy fields.

Successful initiative finalization persists a canonical completedAt timestamp; active and nonterminal authorities cannot carry it, and existing completed schemaVersion 1 files without it remain readable under an explicit backward-compatibility rule.

The prune planner discovers only validated canonical complete initiatives, computes age from completedAt, inventories all initiative files, classifies Git-tracked and ignored/untracked content, and returns deterministic eligible/skipped reasons without mutation.

Prune apply removes only entries authorized by the current project/user retention policy and explicit apply request, revalidates lock, symlink, status, timestamp, inventory fingerprint, and tracked-content constraints immediately before deletion, and fails closed on races or ambiguity.

Tracked workflow authority and durable reviewed artifacts are skipped by default; optional includeTracked only exposes them to explicit apply, leaves Git-visible deletions uncommitted, and never pushes.
Routine completions and initiative suggestions omit completed initiatives by default while explicit status/open/completed-history access remains available and bounded.

Documentation states configuration, completion-clock compatibility, dry-run/apply semantics, tracked-content behavior, irreversibility, recovery expectations, and the distinction between ignored log cleanup and whole-initiative pruning.

Focused config, lifecycle, discovery, Git-classification, symlink, lock, race, dry-run, apply, and negative tests pass together with typecheck, repository checks, command inventory, and the full test suite.

assessment.reason: The feature introduces project/user configuration, a lifecycle schema addition, destructive filesystem operations, Git-aware retention decisions, concurrent-state checks, and public command/tool behavior. Preview-first delivery and strict fail-closed boundaries are required.
surfaces: pi-swe initiative schema and completion transition
unknowns: The exact schemaVersion 1 compatibility representation for missing completedAt must avoid rewriting historical authorities merely to make them pruneable.
Git classification should use the narrowest permission-preserving read path while remaining deterministic for unusual filenames and repositories without Git.
The best explicit completed-history syntax should reuse the existing action grammar without overloading the current per-topic list action.
Whether ignored logs-only automatic cleanup provides enough value to justify a background/session-start path should be decided after planner performance and safety tests.

practices.reason: A durable completion clock is necessary, but existing tracked completed authorities must remain readable and immutable unless deliberately migrated.
Retention belongs at user/project scope and should follow an already-qualified Gentic configuration model rather than inventing initiative-local settings.
Pruning can irreversibly remove ignored local history and create tracked Git deletions, so candidate planning and apply must be separate and race-safe.
Tracked workflow authority and reviewed artifacts have different retention value from ignored runtime logs and must be skipped by default.
Hiding completed initiatives from routine suggestions solves common clutter while explicit history access preserves inspection.
Schema, configuration, destructive boundaries, command guidance, and documentation require integrated review and regression evidence.

obligations.text: Test canonical completedAt creation, terminal-state invariants, intentional revision behavior, old completed-authority readability, and rejection of malformed or contradictory timestamps.
Test safe bounded global/project config precedence, disabled defaults, unknown/malformed fields, oversized files, symlinks, and bounded diagnostics.

Exercise deterministic dry-run planning and explicit apply across complete, nonterminal, malformed, locked, symlinked, changed-after-plan, and large bounded initiative sets, proving no mutation during preview and fail-closed deletion under races.

Use isolated Git repositories to verify tracked/ignored/untracked classification, default tracked skips, explicit includeTracked candidate behavior, preservation of unrelated files, uncommitted Git-visible deletions, and absence of push behavior.
Test root/action/topic completions and list/history output so completed initiatives are hidden from routine flows but remain explicitly inspectable, bounded, and tolerant of malformed state.
Run typecheck, repository checks, command inventory, focused pi-swe suites, and the full suite after documentation and generated inventory are current.

Perform a source-bound model self-review of configuration precedence, schema compatibility, deletion containment, race handling, Git semantics, command clarity, boundedness, and documentation accuracy.

work.title: Add completedAt lifecycle semantics and project/user retention configuration

testing.approach: Characterize current completed authorities and configuration conventions, add backward-compatible schema/lifecycle tests and config negative fixtures first, then implement canonical finalization timestamps and bounded global/project merging.
testing.reason: Reliable age-based retention needs durable lifecycle time and safe opt-in configuration before any pruning logic exists.

work.title: Build the preview-first Git-aware prune planner and race-safe explicit executor

testing.approach: Construct isolated filesystem and Git fixtures for every eligibility and skip reason, lock/symlink/race condition, unusual filename, tracked-content mode, and bounded-set limit; prove dry-run byte stability before implementing apply.
testing.reason: Candidate selection and destructive execution must be independently testable, deterministic, and fail closed immediately before deletion.

work.title: Integrate prune and completed-history surfaces, documentation, review, and qualification

testing.approach: Add command/tool and autocomplete characterization for routine-hidden versus explicit completed views, update documentation and inventory, perform source-bound review, then run focused and full repository gates.
testing.reason: The retention engine is useful only when safely discoverable, accurately explained, and qualified across existing pi-swe behavior.

decisions.text: Completed-initiative retention is a pi-swe-owned project/user policy, not an initiative-level policy or separate extension.
decisions.basis: User preference and pi-swe's existing ownership of initiative schema, status, paths, and locks.

decisions.text: Dry-run is the default; whole-initiative deletion always requires explicit apply.
decisions.basis: Whole-directory pruning can delete ignored local history and create tracked Git deletions.

decisions.text: Tracked workflow authority and reviewed artifacts are skipped by default; includeTracked only affects explicit apply and never commits or pushes.
decisions.basis: Repository artifact policy treats completed tracked authority as durable review history.

decisions.text: Age-based retention uses canonical completedAt, never filesystem mtime or ignored revision-log names.
decisions.basis: Portable deterministic pruning requires a timestamp in durable authority.

decisions.text: Routine discovery hides completed initiatives without deleting them; explicit history access remains available.
decisions.basis: Most day-to-day clutter can be reduced without destructive action.

decisions.text: Any automatic behavior considered during implementation is limited to ignored logs-only cleanup; whole-initiative pruning remains explicit.
decisions.basis: Preserve normal destructive-operation authorization and avoid silent loss of untracked durable material.

risks.text: Deleting an initiative directory can lose ignored revision history or untracked artifacts that Git cannot restore.
risks.mitigation: Preview every file classification, require explicit apply, skip ambiguity, and document irreversibility.

risks.text: Tracked authority deletion can silently become part of a later unrelated commit.
risks.mitigation: Skip tracked content by default; when explicitly included, report Git-visible deletions prominently and never commit automatically.

risks.text: A concurrent writer or symlink swap can redirect or invalidate pruning after preview.
risks.mitigation: Use stable directory handles, exclusive locks, inventory fingerprints, immediate revalidation, parent-relative deletion, and directory sync.

risks.text: Adding completedAt could invalidate or reject historical schemaVersion 1 authorities.
risks.mitigation: Define and test an explicit read-compatible missing-field rule while enforcing timestamp invariants for new finalizations.

risks.text: Large initiative sets or Git classification can slow completion and command UX.
risks.mitigation: Bound discovery and output, avoid background whole-tree deletion, and measure planner performance with maximum-size fixtures.

risks.text: Hiding completed initiatives could make history appear lost.
risks.mitigation: Provide explicit completed/history filters and keep direct status/open access by canonical topic.
